newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks plummet on Kia bail-out news.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks plummet on Kia bail-out news.

text.p: The South Korean stock market fell 2.00 percent in early afternoon trading on Tuesday on the news the nation's eighth-largest Kia Group had been designated for bail-out, brokers said.
The composite stock index was down 15.31 points at 749.14 at 0500 GMT.
The nation's eighth-largest conglomerate, the Kia Group, has been designated for bail-out, a central Bank of Korea spokesman said on Tuesday.
Creditor banks to the group, whose flagship unit is Kia Motors Corp, were due to officially announce details at 0530 GMT, the spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
Kia has been troubled by worsening cash flow problems because financial institutions, alarmed by two major corporate collapses earlier this year, have tightened credit lines.
An official at the Kia Group's public information department declined to comment on the news of the bail-out.
All six listed Kia Group shares went limit down in early afternoon trading, brokers said.
The flagship carmaker Kia Motors lost 1,100 won to 13,400 and commercial vehicle producer Asia Motors shed 300 won to 3,550.

"Investors began dumping their holdings of Kia shares," said a Tongyang Securities broker. "Investors believed the news proved long-standing rumours that Kia had had serious financial difficulties despite constant denials by the group."
Park Joo-chang at Daewoo Securities said: "Now, nobody will believe either the government or business groups when they deny financial problems."
Brokers said jittery investors renewed their concerns about further financial troubles of other big groups.
